note: Majority: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 11 of the Laws of Antigua and Barbuda (in force 13 December 1984), section 2: a person attains full age at eighteen instead of twenty-one; section 13 lets a person over sixteen consent to medical treatment. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: Antigua and Barbuda Labour Code, Cap. 27 (revised edition on laws.gov.ag), Division E (Women, Young Persons and Children (Employment)), section E2: a child is a person under fourteen and a young person one under eighteen who is no longer a child; section E3(1): no child may be employed or work in a public or private agricultural or industrial undertaking or on a ship, save family undertakings, youth-organisation fund-raising and work beside adult family members (outside school hours, at most eight hours a day, thirty a week, never at night); section E5: a young person is employed only after a medical examination. Employment of Children Prohibition Act, Cap. 151 (No. 5 of 1939, amended 32/1956; on laws.gov.ag), sections 2 and 3: no one may employ in any occupation whatsoever a child, there a person under twelve, save light domestic or agricultural work at home for the parents or guardian. So the general age is 12, and 14 in agricultural and industrial undertakings and on ships (my reading of the two together). Performers: neither Act names an exception or licence for performing, so barred under twelve (my reading); this should be checked, as should amendments after the revised editions, which weren't looked for. Service: no Defence Act was found in laws.gov.ag's alphabetical or chapter lists, so no source on a call-up was read; null.

sources.said: "child" means a person who in the opinion of the Court, in a prosecution for an offence against this Act, is under the age of twelve years
